NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>SOURCE 1–2 show the same elongated building from its ramped short end and adjoining long side: a recessed lower frame, projecting two-level glazed enclosure, zigzag exterior ramps and a concave timber roof with unequal edge heights. SOURCE 3 shows the glazed entrance and an open gallery beneath grating supported by transverse beams. SOURCE 4 shows the curved timber ceiling, guarded circular floor openings, spiral stair and lower concrete-framed workspace. SOURCE 5–8 establish the perimeter buffer, retained frame, added upper hall and differing floor/void relationships through sections, exploded diagrams and plans; these are not exterior cutaway views. CURRENT captures the broad arrangement, but reverses defining end relationships, substitutes solid gallery construction and leaves a visible floor opening unguarded. No confirmed dimensions are supplied. The blank lower-interior image and repeated uncut views cannot verify internal floor connections or concealed joints.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="end">problem: SOURCE 1’s end views show the roof’s right edge higher than its left and the upper ramp descending toward the right. CURRENT 15 shows the opposite roof-edge hierarchy and upper-ramp direction. Ramp/rail extensions also project beyond the enclosure without clearly resolved landing connections.
action: Locally correct the roof edge heights and ramp handedness against the same source end landmarks. Trim extensions and connect each flight to its corresponding landing with continuous walking surfaces and guards; preserve the established concave roof concept.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="gallery">problem: SOURCE 3 shows a light, permeable grating deck overhead with distinct transverse support beams. CURRENT 19 presents a continuous solid soffit with no comparable exposed beam rhythm. CURRENT 16–18 also read as heavy dark railing grids and opaque horizontal bands, obscuring the source’s light glazed buffer and open gallery.
action: Patch the gallery deck to show the source-backed grating and exposed support bays. Reduce excessive rail/frame bulk and apply the observed pale frame finish and transparent glazing, retaining actual floor-edge structure.</issue>
<issue priority="3" view="interior">problem: SOURCE 4 shows mesh guards surrounding the visible circular floor openings. CURRENT 20 has a large foreground opening with no perimeter guard, while the farther stair opening has a coarse bar enclosure. The foreground opening’s exact placement cannot be confirmed from this camera.
action: Add a continuous mesh guard around the exposed foreground opening and refine the stair-opening guard to the source’s light assembly. Check opening locations against SOURCE 7 before changing their positions; verify that stair flights terminate at real floor openings.</issue>
<keep>
The roof’s continuous concave curvature.
The upper hall’s visible timber ceiling material zone.
The repeated pale columns along the lower glazed frontage.
</keep>
